messages.Modifică parametrii și urmărește mișcare: Change the parameters and observe the moving particle, its component oscillations and the Lissajous curve.
messages.Selectarea unui raport aplică pulsații e: Selecting a ratio applies exact angular frequencies. Phase and amplitudes can then be adjusted.
messages.Două tonuri sintetizate, asociate celor: Two synthesized tones represent the two oscillations. Audio frequencies are scaled for hearing and do not represent the physical angular frequencies.
messages.Verde: laturi verticale. Galben: laturi: Green: vertical sides. Yellow: horizontal sides. White: corner.
messages.Figura Lissajous în planul xOy: Lissajous figure in the xOy plane
messages.Aplicație educațională offline · Unități: Offline educational application · Arbitrary coordinate units · Angular frequencies in rad/s
messages.Un punct material efectuează simultan do: A particle simultaneously performs two harmonic oscillations along mutually perpendicular directions Ox and Oy. Its position vector is the sum of the two displacements, and its endpoint traces a planar trajectory.
messages.Aₓ și Aᵧ reprezintă amplitudinile, ωₓ și: Aₓ and Aᵧ are the amplitudes, ωₓ and ωᵧ the angular frequencies in rad/s, and φₓ and φᵧ the initial phases. In the simulator the time origin is chosen so that φₓ = 0, and the initial phase along Oy is denoted by Δφ. For equal angular frequencies this is the constant phase difference. For different angular frequencies the instantaneous difference is (ωᵧ − ωₓ)t + Δφ. For equal angular frequencies, shifting the time origin does not change the trajectory. For different angular frequencies, φₓ = 0 is a simulator convention; the initial phases determine the figure and starting point.
messages.Pulsații egale: ωₓ = ωᵧ = ω: Equal angular frequencies: ωₓ = ωᵧ = ω
messages.Eliminând timpul din ecuațiile parametri: Eliminating time from the parametric equations gives the general trajectory equation:
messages.Pentru amplitudini nenule, aceasta descr: For nonzero amplitudes this generally describes an ellipse. Special cases for Aₓ > 0 and Aᵧ > 0:
messages.Segmentul y = (Aᵧ/Aₓ)x, situat în cadran: The segment y = (Aᵧ/Aₓ)x in quadrants I and III, traversed in both directions
messages.Segmentul y = −(Aᵧ/Aₓ)x, situat în cadra: The segment y = −(Aᵧ/Aₓ)x in quadrants II and IV, traversed in both directions
messages.Elipsă cu semiaxele Aₓ și Aᵧ, paralele c: Ellipse with semiaxes Aₓ and Aᵧ parallel to the coordinate axes. Clockwise at +90° and counterclockwise at −90°
messages.Cerc cu raza Aₓ. Sens orar la +90° și an: Circle with radius Aₓ. Clockwise at +90° and counterclockwise at −90°
messages.Elipsă, de regulă înclinată față de axe: An ellipse, usually tilted relative to the axes
messages.Perioada este T = 2π/ω. Pentru Δφ = 0°,: The period is T = 2π/ω. At Δφ = 0°, y = (Aᵧ/Aₓ)x. The coordinates always have the same sign, so the segment lies in quadrants I and III. At Δφ = 180°, y = −(Aᵧ/Aₓ)x. The coordinates have opposite signs, so the segment lies in quadrants II and IV. The origin O belongs to both segments but to no quadrant.
messages.Pentru o elipsă sau un cerc, sensul de p: For an ellipse or circle the traversal direction is determined by the sign of sin(Δφ), for ω > 0 with Ox pointing right and Oy pointing up. For 0° < Δφ < 180° the motion is clockwise. For −180° < Δφ < 0° it is counterclockwise. At Δφ = 0° or ±180° the trajectory is a segment without a single traversal direction.
messages.Această expresie este proporțională cu v: This expression is proportional to the signed areal velocity. A negative sign indicates clockwise motion and a positive sign counterclockwise motion. Positive amplitudes change the shape and size of the ellipse, not its traversal direction. Reversing the sign of the common angular frequency would reverse the motion, but the simulator uses positive angular frequencies. The common initial phase sets the starting point on the curve, not the traversal direction.
The trajectory is called a Lissajous figure. For a rational angular-frequency ratio ωᵧ/ωₓ = p/q, where p and q are coprime positive integers, the figure is closed and the motion repeats after a common period:
messages.Exemple: raporturile 1:2, 2:3 și 3:4 pro: Examples: ratios 1:2, 2:3 and 3:4 produce different Lissajous figures. The phase difference changes the shape and symmetries. The amplitudes change the dimensions along each axis.
messages.Dacă raportul pulsațiilor este irațional: If the angular-frequency ratio is irrational, the trajectory never closes exactly and the motion is quasiperiodic. Over a finite numerical experiment, a rational ratio with a large denominator can resemble an irrational one. The slider supplies decimal values, so all nonzero ratios obtained are mathematically rational. The simulator computes the common period from these decimal values. It draws a complete period only when this does not exceed 120 s.
messages.Punctul roșu reprezintă poziția instanta: The red particle represents the instantaneous position (x(t), y(t)). Its projections onto the axes correspond to the component oscillations. The orange line shows the path travelled during the animation. The blue curve shows a complete short common period, or a limited time interval in other cases.
messages.Graficele inferioare afișează x(t) și y(: The lower graphs display x(t) and y(t) on the same time scale. The vertical cursor marks the shared instant.
messages.Alege pulsații egale, amplitudini egale: Choose equal angular frequencies and amplitudes, then vary the phase difference from 0° to 180°. Identify segments in quadrants I and III or II and IV, ellipses and the circle.
messages.Fixează Δφ = +90° și modifică raportul a: Set Δφ = +90° and vary the amplitude ratio. Observe the change from circle to ellipse and the clockwise motion. Repeat at −90° to reverse the direction.
messages.Compară figurile Lissajous pentru rapoar: Compare Lissajous figures for ratios 1:2, 2:3 and 3:4. Identify the common period.
Choose angular frequencies of 2 rad/s and 2.1 rad/s. Examine the gradual change in the figure.
messages.Dezactivează „Curba teoretică” și urmăre: Turn off the theoretical curve and observe only the travelled path.
messages.ωₓ : ωᵧ = m : n, cu m și n prime între e: ωₓ : ωᵧ = m : n, with m and n coprime
messages.Linia subțire întreruptă delimitează dre: The thin dashed line outlines the rectangle. At x = ±Aₓ the velocity vₓ is zero. If vᵧ is nonzero, the tangent is vertical, parallel to Oy. At y = ±Aᵧ the velocity vᵧ is zero. If vₓ is nonzero, the tangent is horizontal, parallel to Ox.
messages.Într-o perioadă comună, există 2m atinge: In one common period there are 2m contacts with vertical sides and 2n with horizontal sides. These count contact times, not necessarily distinct geometric points. Returning to the same position reduces the number of distinct points. The simulator displays distinct tangencies for each family of sides, corner contacts separately and the total number of contacts in time.
messages.Exemplu: pentru ωₓ : ωᵧ = 1 : 2 și Δφ =: Example: at ωₓ : ωᵧ = 1 : 2 and Δφ = 0°, there are two distinct points on vertical sides and four on horizontal sides. At the same ratio and Δφ = 90°, the curve y/Aᵧ = 1 − 2(x/Aₓ)² has two distinct vertical-side positions and three horizontal-side positions, although the time counts remain 2 and 4.
messages.Un contact în colț, marcat alb, anulează: At a corner contact, shown in white, both vₓ and vᵧ vanish. This is not a regular tangency with either side. For example, the segments for equal angular frequencies at phase 0° or 180° reach two corners and reverse there. Tangency counters exclude corners. Total time counts include corner contacts.
messages.Pentru raportul 3:4 și Δφ = 90°, figura: At ratio 3:4 and Δφ = 90° the figure has 2 vertical tangencies, 3 horizontal tangencies and 2 contacts at the upper corners. Including corners, there are 4 vertical-side and 5 horizontal-side contact positions. In time, there are 6 vertical-side and 8 horizontal-side contacts in a common period.
messages.Verde indică tangențele la laturile vert: Green marks tangencies with vertical sides. Yellow marks tangencies with horizontal sides. White marks corner contacts. For periods over 120 s, complete markers are omitted and the curve shows a finite interval. The period is calculated exactly from the decimal angular frequencies.
messages.Comutatorul de simetrie evidențiază axel: The symmetry switch highlights Ox and Oy in purple when the figure is invariant under the corresponding reflection. A purple circle at the origin indicates central symmetry. Symmetries are calculated for the complete figure from its frequency ratio and phase, even while the travelled path is incomplete. Tilted ellipses also have their own symmetry axes, which are not highlighted here.
messages.Săgeata albă indică direcția vitezei ins: The white arrow indicates the instantaneous velocity direction. For figures with loops, follow the local direction on each branch. The whole figure has no single clockwise or counterclockwise direction. At zero total speed the arrow disappears.
messages.Activează oprirea automată și apasă Cont: Enable automatic pausing and press Continue. The animation stops exactly when either component reaches an extremum. Next extremum advances directly to the next such instant. The text displays coordinates and velocity components. Use this feature to check tangent orientation and corner contacts.
messages.Parametri modificați manual. Explorează: Parameters changed manually. Explore the trajectory.
messages.În fază: segmentul traversează cadranele: In phase: the segment crosses quadrants I and III (x and y have the same sign).
messages.În opoziție de fază: segmentul traversea: Opposite phase: the segment crosses quadrants II and IV (x and y have opposite signs).
messages.Cerc parcurs în sens orar pentru Δφ = +9: Clockwise circle at Δφ = +90°, with Ox pointing right and Oy pointing up.
messages.Elipsă cu axele paralele cu Ox și Oy, pa: Ellipse with axes parallel to Ox and Oy, traversed clockwise at Δφ = +90°.
messages.Defazajul diferit de 0°, 90° și 180° pro: A phase difference other than 0°, 90° or 180° produces a tilted ellipse.
messages.O figură Lissajous închisă pentru pulsaț: A closed Lissajous figure for commensurate angular frequencies.
messages.Figura formează bucle caracteristice rap: The figure forms loops characteristic of ratio 2:3.
messages.O figură periodică cu structură mai boga: A periodic figure with a richer structure.
messages.Defazajul schimbă forma figurii, nu rapo: The phase changes the figure shape, not the angular-frequency ratio.
messages.O figură închisă cu amplitudini diferite: A closed figure with different amplitudes.
messages.Figura se modifică lent, iar perioada co: The figure changes slowly and the common period is long.

messages.De unde vine numele „Figuri Lissajous”?: Where does the name “Lissajous figures” come from?
messages.Figurile poartă numele fizicianului fran: The figures are named after the French physicist Jules Antoine Lissajous (1822–1880), who used optical methods to study combined vibrations. In his apparatus, a light beam was reflected successively by two mirrors mounted on tuning forks vibrating in perpendicular directions. The light spot traced the curve produced by the two oscillations on a screen.
messages.Lissajous a demonstrat aceste figuri la: Lissajous demonstrated these figures in Paris in 1855. The curves had previously been studied by Nathaniel Bowditch and are also known as Bowditch curves. “Lissajous” is the researcher’s name, rather than the name of a single geometric shape.
